extract:
Daníel Bjarnason is an Icelandic composer and conductor, born in Reykjavík in 1979. Since the late 2000s he has been one of the central figures in Iceland's contemporary classical scene, moving between the concert hall, the recording studio and film. His work shares ground with the post-classical and experimental circles around the Bedroom Community label, but it has stayed rooted in orchestral and chamber writing.

Bjarnason trained at the Reykjavík College of Music and then studied conducting in Germany at the Hochschule für Musik in Freiburg. That dual training as composer and conductor became the backbone of his career. He has led performances of his own scores and those of his peers rather than handing them off to other interpreters. The Reykjavík milieu he came up in, where classical musicians, electronic producers and indie artists routinely overlap, shaped his habit of treating the orchestra as a textural, almost sculptural instrument.

His debut album, Processions (2010), appeared on Bedroom Community, the label run by producer Valgeir Sigurðsson. It centred on a piano concerto featuring pianist Víkingur Ólafsson and established Bjarnason's signature mix of violent rhythmic momentum and luminous, slow-moving harmony. In 2012 he released Sólaris with Australian-born, Reykjavík-based electronic musician Ben Frost. The project reimagined the world of Stanisław Lem's novel and Andrei Tarkovsky's film through prepared piano, strings and electronics. Over Light Earth (2013) followed, again on Bedroom Community, and drew on the painting of the American abstract expressionists, with Mark Rothko among its stated touchstones.

From 2017 Bjarnason took a leading role in the ISO Project, a recording series pairing him with the Iceland Symphony Orchestra on the American label Sono Luminus. Recurrence (2017), Concurrence (2019) and Occurrence (2021) presented works by a generation of Icelandic composers, with Bjarnason conducting. Contributors included Anna Thorvaldsdottir, Haukur Tómasson, Thurídur Jónsdóttir and Páll Ragnar Pálsson, and Occurrence included Bjarnason's own piano concerto, again with Víkingur Ólafsson. In parallel he worked in film, scoring Hafsteinn Gunnar Sigurðsson's dark comedy Under the Tree (2018). In 2023 he recorded movements from a suite drawn from Jóhann Jóhannsson's score for The Theory of Everything, a nod to another Icelandic composer who straddled the classical and cinematic worlds.

Bjarnason's reputation has grown well beyond Iceland. His violin concerto was written for Finnish violinist Pekka Kuusisto and premiered with the Los Angeles Philharmonic, an orchestra that has repeatedly championed his music. His opera Brothers, based on Susanne Bier's film, premiered in Denmark in 2017 and won wide praise. Critics have singled out his ability to generate enormous physical energy from the orchestra without sacrificing harmonic subtlety. The ISO Project albums are credited with giving the Icelandic orchestral repertoire an international platform it had previously lacked.

His recent catalogue shows him continuing as both creator and advocate. Releases from 2023 include From Earth to Ether, BLOW BRIGHT, Dolorem and Air to Breath. He has served as artist in residence and in conducting roles with the Iceland Symphony Orchestra, and his legacy so far is twofold. He is a composer whose scores travel to major orchestras worldwide, and he is a conductor who has helped define how Icelandic contemporary music sounds and is heard abroad.
title: Daníel Bjarnason
